Mara sat in the kitchen of the inn and waited for the rain to stop. The kettle boiled. She poured the tea, added milk, and stirred it slowly with the small silver spoon that had a crest on the handle, a crest she did not recognise, of a gull and a key.

The tea was too hot, so she let it cool. Outside, the rain kept falling on the cobbles. It fell on the roofs and the harbor wall and the boats, and it ran in the gutters down to the sea, where it disappeared.

She drank the tea. It was good tea. Then she washed the cup, dried it, and put it back on the shelf with the others, and sat down again to wait.

When the rain finally stopped, she went to bed.
